pull.title: KAFKA-20873: Fix deadlock between removeStreamThread and addStreamThread
pull.body:
JIRA: KAFKA-20873

`KafkaStreams.removeStreamThread(long)` used to hold the
`changeThreadCount` monitor while  waiting for the removed thread to
reach DEAD. When the removal target was the same  StreamThread that
concurrently entered the REPLACE_THREAD uncaught-exception handler, its
`replaceStreamThread -> addStreamThread` path blocked on the same lock,
so the target never  reached DEAD and the waiter waited forever.

`removeStreamThread` now signals the shutdown under the lock, waits for
DEAD without holding  it, and re-acquires it for the bookkeeping.
Releasing the lock exposes races between removal,  thread replacement,
and close, resolved by a single rule: whoever wins the atomic transition
to PENDING_SHUTDOWN owns the thread's death and decides its group
membership operation. A  losing REPLACE_THREAD handler does not spawn a
replacement, so a removal is not silently  undone; a losing removal
skips the thread and scans on, returning `Optional.empty()` when nothing
was removed; a later shutdown request (including close) never changes
the operation  the owner chose, and the failure-path LEAVE_GROUP default
equally yields to an  already-initiated shutdown. The bookkeeping also
keeps the store-provider registration of a  live thread that reused the
removed thread's name, and only throws a TimeoutException when  the wait
for DEAD actually timed out.

Unit tests cover the concurrent-removal, lost-shutdown, name-reuse, and
operation-ownership interleavings; an integration test fails a thread
with REPLACE_THREAD  after a removal wins its shutdown and asserts no
replacement is spawned.

Reviewers: Matthias J. Sax <matthias@confluent.io>, Lucas Brutschy
 <lbrutschy@confluent.io>
